title: Console UX copy draft — Quantization Profile warnings + tooltips (route-level enablement)
content:
Context
- Surface area: Console > Routes > {route_name} > Runtime settings > Quantization Profile
- v1 is opt-in and route-level only (per ADR-0137). Default behavior unchanged when Off.
- Console needs to (a) set expectations (quality + determinism), (b) prevent incompatible enablement, (c) make rollback feel safe/obvious, (d) reinforce auditability/RBAC.

Tone goals
- Developer-facing, plain language, no marketing fluff.
- Explicit about risk + reversibility.
- Use consistent terms: “Quantization Profile”, “Baseline precision (default)”, “Fallback”, “Compatibility”.

String conventions / placeholders
- {route_name}, {model_id}, {model_variant}, {profile_id}, {profile_label}, {precision_summary}, {regions}, {deployment_tier}, {gpu_class}, {max_context}, {estimated_savings_pct}
- Avoid implying guarantees: use “may”, “typically”, “expected”, “based on Redwood benchmarks”.

1) Toggle label + helper text
A. Toggle label options
1) “Enable Quantization Profile”
2) “Use quantized execution”
3) “Run with Quantization Profile (opt-in)”

B. Helper text options (under toggle)
Option B1 (short)
- “Reduce cost by running this route with an approved quantization profile. You can roll back instantly.”

Option B2 (medium)
- “Run this route with an approved quantization profile to reduce cost. Compatibility is validated at save time; incompatible requests fall back to baseline.”

Option B3 (more explicit)
- “Quantization profiles reduce cost by lowering numeric precision for supported models/hardware. Output may change. You can disable at any time; baseline remains available.”

2) Profile picker: tooltip + empty state
A. Picker label options
1) “Quantization profile”
2) “Profile selection”
3) “Profile (versioned)”

B. Tooltip for picker (info icon)
Option T1
- “Profiles are versioned and model-specific. The runtime applies the selected profile deterministically when compatible.”

Option T2
- “Choose a versioned profile for {model_id}/{model_variant}. If a request is incompatible (e.g., GPU class or context), Redwood falls back to baseline.”

Option T3 (mentions audit)
- “Your selection is recorded in audit logs. The runtime uses this exact profile version unless you change it.”

C. Empty state when no profiles available
Option E1
- “No approved profiles available for this model variant.”

Option E2
- “No profiles published for {model_id}/{model_variant} yet. Contact support if you need coverage.”

Option E3 (actionable)
- “No compatible profiles found for the selected model + deployment. Try another region/tier or switch back to baseline.”

3) Compatibility warning (blocking vs non-blocking)
Notes
- Some compatibility issues should block save (hard incompatibility for the route’s pinned model/tier), others can be warn-only (known caveats that still allow fallback).

A. Hard-block (cannot enable)
Option C-H1 (short)
- “This profile isn’t compatible with the current deployment configuration.”

Option C-H2 (specific)
- “Incompatible: {profile_id} doesn’t support {gpu_class} or {max_context} for {model_variant}. Choose a different profile or use baseline.”

Option C-H3 (with remediation)
- “Can’t enable: this profile is not approved for {deployment_tier} in {regions}. Switch region/tier or select another profile.”

B. Warn-only (fallback expected for some requests)
Option C-W1
- “Some requests may fall back to baseline due to compatibility constraints (GPU class, context length, or kernel support).”

Option C-W2 (adds observability hint)
- “Fallback may occur for requests exceeding profile limits. Monitor ‘fallback_rate’ after enabling.”

Option C-W3 (adds determinism)
- “Selection is deterministic per request: the runtime will either apply {profile_label} or fall back to baseline. No partial application.”

C. Microcopy for “Why?” link (opens popover)
Option WHY1
- “Compatibility is checked against your pinned model variant, deployment tier, and regional hardware. If any constraint isn’t met, Redwood falls back to baseline.”

Option WHY2
- “Profiles have limits (e.g., max context, GPU requirements, supported kernels). Redwood enforces these limits to avoid incorrect execution.”

4) Quality risk warning (always shown when enabling)
A. Inline warning banner (non-blocking)
Option Q1 (short)
- “Output may change when quantization is enabled.”

Option Q2 (recommended)
- “Quantization can change outputs. Run your evals before enabling broadly.”

Option Q3 (explicit + reversible)
- “Quantization may change outputs and quality. Enable on a canary route first and roll back if you see regressions.”

B. Tooltip / expanded text (for “Learn more”)
Option Q-EXP1
- “Quantization reduces precision to lower cost and may change token probabilities. Redwood runs offline benchmarks, but you should validate on your prompts and success metrics.”

Option Q-EXP2 (ties to guardrails)
- “Profiles are published only after Redwood evals pass internal thresholds, but your workload may differ. Consider A/B testing and monitoring quality signals.”

Option Q-EXP3 (mentions structured outputs/tool calling)
- “If you rely on strict formatting, tool calling, or structured output constraints, verify behavior with your prompts. Small probability shifts can affect formatting reliability.”

5) “Experimental” / “Deprecated” profile labels
A. Experimental badge tooltip
Option EXP1
- “Experimental profiles may change or be withdrawn based on new eval results. Use for testing, not default production traffic.”

Option EXP2
- “Experimental: quality/perf data is limited. Expect higher fallback or more variance. Roll back if metrics regress.”

B. Deprecated badge tooltip
Option DEP1
- “Deprecated: this profile will be removed on {deprecation_date}. Migrate to a newer version.”

Option DEP2
- “Deprecated due to updated benchmarks or constraints. We recommend switching to {recommended_profile_id}.”

6) Rollback + kill-switch messaging
A. Rollback helper text (near toggle)
Option R1 (short)
- “Disable to revert to baseline immediately.”

Option R2 (adds propagation expectation)
- “Disabling reverts to baseline. Changes usually propagate within ~{prop_seconds}s.”

Option R3 (adds incident framing)
- “If you see regressions, disable the profile to revert to baseline. For widespread issues, Redwood may also apply a platform kill-switch.”

B. Confirmation modal when enabling (first time per route)
Title options
1) “Enable quantization for {route_name}?”
2) “Confirm quantization profile enablement”

Body options
Modal M1 (balanced)
- “This route will attempt to use {profile_label} ({precision_summary}). Outputs may change. If a request is incompatible, Redwood will fall back to baseline.

Recommended: enable on a canary route and monitor latency, error rate, and fallback rate.”

Modal M2 (more direct)
- “You’re changing execution precision for this route. This can affect output quality and latency.

You can roll back at any time by disabling the profile.”

Modal M3 (includes audit)
- “This change will be recorded in audit logs (actor, time, route, and profile version). Proceed?”

Buttons
- Primary: “Enable profile”
- Secondary: “Cancel”
- Optional link: “View compatibility details”

C. Confirmation modal when switching profile versions
Title
- “Switch profile version?”

Body options
Switch S1
- “You’re switching from {old_profile_id} to {new_profile_id}. Outputs and performance may change. Consider canarying this change.”

Switch S2 (mentions silent changes)
- “Profile versions are pinned. Switching updates the pinned version used by the runtime.”

7) Audit log / change history microcopy
A. Section label
1) “Change history”
2) “Audit log”
3) “Configuration history”

B. Helper text
Option A1
- “Shows who changed quantization settings and when.”

Option A2
- “Includes route, profile version, and enable/disable events.”

Option A3 (compliance tone)
- “Recorded for compliance. Export available via Audit Log API.”

C. Event row text (examples)
- “{actor} enabled quantization profile {profile_id} on {route_name}”
- “{actor} switched profile from {old_profile_id} to {new_profile_id}”
- “{actor} disabled quantization (baseline)”
- “System applied global kill-switch (quantization disabled)”

8) Metrics + observability nudges (non-intrusive)
A. Post-save toast (success)
Option O1
- “Saved. Monitor fallback rate and p95 latency for {route_name}.”

Option O2
- “Saved. View quantization rollout dashboard.”

B. Inline “Monitor” link tooltip
- “Opens dashboards filtered to this route (enabled rate, fallback rate, latency, errors, and cost/token deltas).”

9) Error states (API / save)
A. RBAC
Option RB1
- “You don’t have permission to change quantization settings for this route.”

Option RB2
- “Insufficient permissions. Ask a project admin to update route runtime settings.”

B. Feature flag / allowlist
Option FF1
- “Quantization Profile Library isn’t enabled for your organization.”

Option FF2
- “This feature is currently in beta and requires enablement. Contact support to join.”

C. Save blocked due to compatibility
Option SB1
- “Can’t save: selected profile is incompatible with this route’s model/deployment settings.”

Option SB2
- “Can’t save: {profile_id} exceeds max context ({max_context}). Choose a compatible profile or use baseline.”

D. Backend transient failure (profile metadata fetch)
Option BE1
- “Couldn’t load profile details. Try again.”

Option BE2 (more actionable)
- “We couldn’t fetch profile metadata right now. Your route is unchanged. Retry in a minute, or contact support if this persists.”

10) Proposed default copy set (if we pick one path)
- Toggle helper: B2
- Enable modal: M1
- Compatibility warn: C-W2
- Quality warning: Q2
- Rollback helper: R2

Open questions / TODO
- Do we want to show estimated savings ({estimated_savings_pct}) in-product for v1? If yes, copy needs careful hedging (“based on Redwood benchmarks; your mileage may vary”).
- Do we expose aliases like “recommended/latest” in Console? If yes, add warning about pinned vs alias behavior (see Slack thread re: avoiding silent changes).
- If a route spans multiple regions, do we show a per-region compatibility breakdown inline or only behind “View details”?

Notes from review (03/10)
- Dylan: keep it short on the main screen; push details into popovers.
- Arjun: always mention that output may change; do not imply zero-quality-risk.
- Connor: include a clear rollback statement and propagation expectation.
- Naomi: ensure audit log language is explicit and non-optional.
